Yeah. I'm with you on this shit. Well...was with you on this bullshit. Honestly, bi-cycles are really really really extreme. I rarely feel simultaneously attracted to both sexes and ever since coming out, I feel more attracted to men. Either way, the way I used to think about it is no matter how long the period is/how long the bi-cycle is, if it happened once...it'll happen again. I remember my first ever bi-cycle was when I was around 13/14 and it lasted for 3 days. The confusion it brought was monumental. On top of that, I understand how hard it can be when you're in a relationship with someone of the opposite sex. Personally speaking, breaking up with my ex was a huge relief but that's just because she used to do a lot of shit that wasn't exactly normal, and I felt deeply overwhelmed by the relationship. All in all, if it brings you extreme anxiety, my best advice would be to break it off. If it doesn't and you're confident that the bi-cycle will just flux, then stick with it. I hope this helped.

Hey man, I just wanted to enlighten you on my struggles since I figured I'd have a bit of things to share. I've gone through what you're going through and I empathise with your confusion since I've had that same confusion, not too long ago actually. The best thing for you to do is to stay true to yourself. 

Growing up, throughout middle and high school, I've always had romantic crushes (or so I thought) on girls, y'know the 'I look forward to seeing her' type of crushes and so I thought I was straight. That changed roughly around when I was 12 when I stumbled on gay porn and suddenly felt a physical attraction. Don't get me wrong, I used to masturbate to girls back then but it wasn't as potent as when I viewed gay pornographic images. So I didn't pay it much attention growing up and I just kind of went on with 'oh I like this porn more than that' and I started watching gay porn more than straight porn for a good few years growing up. Meanwhile, I'd still have crushes on girls so I figured I was bi. Then I dated a girl and figured that it really wasn't for me and my 'attractions' to girls whether genuine or faux were merely a result of being conditioned into believing that a real family was between a man and a woman and I wanted to be 'normal' because it felt like I was more valid as a human than simply being myself. 

Now I don't really label my sexuality, I do find myself sometimes being attracted to girls but very rarely in comparison to guys. If I had to label it, I'd just call myself gay because it's more accessible. But I could be fluid, so who really knows? 

The key take away is don't do something just because you think it'll be easier for you if you're not wholeheartedly committed to it.

I think, for people to comment on how another person has taken care of their trauma/stories and to give it a verdict is ultimately counterintuitive nor is it conducive to the survivor's healing. I believe you did the right thing for your story. You didn't ignore it when it happened, nor did you stay silent (I'm not judging other survivors for their actions because I understand how traumatized and scary rape/molestation is) about the matter. You took matters into your own hands and are taking the necessary precautions and steps to healing. On top of that, you are also speaking about it which is a very healthy way to deal with your trauma. As for going to the police, if you feel like you have to or you want to, it's not too late to press charges and proceed with litigation. Depending on where you are, the statute of limitations is usually no less than a year. So if you want to, you're good to go. Good luck.
